ideas.title: Tired pots you can see: green iron clouds at the bars
ideas.critique: It shows a hidden state that is already solved and adds one tool, which is a real step past pots that sit there. But 'stirring resets the layer to the bulk' is a switch, not a flow that thins delta, and the film is another dusk close-up of jars whose payoff is a cart that goes further.

ideas.title: Hear the motor work: sound from the solved current
ideas.nearest: Chipping a stone to change its note
ideas.critique: Sound driven by commutation, spark energy and belt slip is a new sense for the cart, and it is the most surprising thing here. The mapping from those numbers to hum, noise and band-pass squeal is a synth patch someone chose, not solved acoustics, and until the cart can be driven the player only listens.

ideas.title: Cart run: a mini game to stop the cart on the flag
ideas.critique: It finally hands the cart to the player, with two choices that the solved motor and rolling resistance decide. A random flag with three tries is a standard menu mini game, and stopping the motor by a clip that pulls off when the cord runs out is a rig that sets distance by cord length, not by the charge.

ideas.title: Lumi winds the field coil with its beak
ideas.nearest: A copper wire keeps its bends
ideas.critique: Lumi's own body doing the work and a turn count the motor really answers is what the human keeps asking for. Revealing a path laid in advance up to the wound length is an animation of geometry that already exists, not wire laid by tension, and beak IK on a crank will slide unless it is held for real.

ideas.title: A drag race: stones against the wound field
ideas.critique: Two solved torque tables on the same pots is an honest comparison, and the flat versus rise crossover is a good result if the physics really gives it. The berry bet and the friends dropping the flag are decoration, and a second road and cart cost a lot for one comparison you watch once.

ideas.title: A cup anemometer that writes down yesterday's wind
ideas.critique: Counting pebbles for the wind is charming. But it is a new instrument prop with Cd numbers written in, it records the wind without charging anything, and the player has nothing to decide once the cups spin.

ideas.title: The dynamo lights a wire red
ideas.critique: A wire glowing red to orange and then burning through is the same shot as 'Where I rushed it', only fed by a crank. Back-torque on the crank and resistance rising with temperature are the new parts, and they matter only if the player feels them.

ideas.title: The friends climb aboard and the cart feels it
ideas.critique: It is a big-goal step, but the payoff is the friends' weight and a stall, which is a riding gag. Mass is just added to the cart and the rear wheel's load, so the physics hardly changes, and 'change the pulley' is the same choice the mini game would already give.

ideas.title: Forming lead plates over days
ideas.critique: A daily rhythm where skipped days show is a real game loop, and the accumulator is a core part of the cart. A time-lapse of plates changing colour is a slow film, and a layer that grows a set amount per cycle's charge, with gas past full charge drawn as bubbles, is a fitted curve unless the electrochemistry is solved.

ideas.title: A dusk lamp on the cart from its own axle
ideas.critique: A light whose brightness comes from a solved filament temperature is a fine Hikari showpiece, and the bobbing beam will look good. It is the third dusk lamp or glowing wire film, and it gives the player nothing to choose.
